extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, courts, merchants, manufacturers, and others concerned with compliance and enforcement under the Merchandise Marks Act 1862 (UK)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the statutory standards, offences, duties, and remedies under the Merchandise Marks Act 1862 governing fraudulent marking, use, sale, and description of trade marks and marked goods. Covers definitions, criminal offences, penalties, civil remedies, procedural rules, and vendor warranties arising under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction/Definitions: 'Person', 'mark', 'Trade Mark', 'misdemeanor', 'court' (s.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the construction of this Act the word 'Person' shall include any person, whether a subject of Her Majesty or not, and any body corporate or body of the like nature... the word 'mark' shall include any name, signature, word, letter, device, emblem, figure, sign, seal, stamp, diagram, label, ticket, or other mark of any other description; and the expression 'Trade Mark' shall include any and every such ... mark lawfully used by any person to denote any chattel ... or to be an article of any peculiar or particular description made or sold by such person; the word 'misdemeanor' shall include crime and offence in Scotland; and the word 'court' shall include any sheriff or sheriff substitute in Scotland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides broad, inclusive statutory definitions so that corporate bodies, foreign entities, various types of marks, and Scottish terminology are within the Act's scope; use these definitions when interpreting offences and duties under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence: Forging/counterfeiting or applying forged/counterfeit trade mark with intent to defraud (s.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who, with intent to defraud, or to enable another to defraud, shall forge or counterfeit, or cause or procure to be forged or counterfeited, any trade mark, or shall apply ... any forged or counterfeited trade mark to any chattel or article not being the manufacture ... of the person denoted by such trade mark, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty includes forfeiture to Her Majesty of every chattel and article to which the false mark was applied, and every instrument used for applying such marks; the court may order forfeited articles to be destroyed or otherwise disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence: Applying forged/counterfeit mark to vessels, cases, wrappers, labels, etc. (s.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who, with intent to defraud, shall apply or cause or procure to be applied any trade mark or any forged or counterfeited trade mark to any cask, bottle, stopper, vessel, case, cover, wrapper, band, reel, ticket, label, or other thing in, on, or with which any chattel or article shall be intended to be sold or uttered or exposed for sale ... shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forfeiture provisions extend to such containers, wrappers, tickets, labels, instruments for applying marks, and similar items; the court may order destroyed or disposed of forfeited items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence: Selling or exposing for sale articles together with forged/counterfeit trade marks, knowing them to be forged (s.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who ... shall sell, utter, or expose ... any chattel or article, together with any forged or counterfeited trade mark, which he shall know to be forged or counterfeited, or together with the trade mark of any other person applied or used falsely or wrongfully or without lawful authority or excuse, shall for every such offence forfeit and pay to Her Majesty a sum equal to the value of the chattel or article and a further sum not exceeding five pounds and not less than ten shillings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution may be compromised (note); applies whether the false mark is on the article itself or on its container/label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additions/alterations/imitations of trade marks with intent to defraud deemed forgeries (s.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every addition to and every alteration of, and also every imitation of any trade mark which shall be made, applied, or used with intent to defraud, or which shall cause a trade mark with such alteration or addition or such imitation to resemble any genuine trade mark so as to be calculated or likely to deceive, shall be and be deemed to be a false, forged and counterfeited trade mark within the meaning of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts of making, applying, or otherwise using such alterations or imitations with intent to defraud are treated as forging and counterfeiting for enforcement and penalty purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to give information where person sold article having a false trade mark (s.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person ... shall have sold, uttered, or exposed for sale ... any chattel or article together with any forged or counterfeited trade mark ... such person shall be bound upon demand in writing by or on behalf of any person whose trade mark shall have been so forged or counterfeited, to give within forty-eight hours full information in writing of the name and address of the person from whom he purchased or obtained such chattel or article and of the time when he obtained the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A justice may summon a refuser; refusal or neglect to comply shall forfeit £5 and such refusal is prima facie evidence of knowledge that the mark was forged/used without authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence: False marking or false descriptive statements on articles or their containers (s.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who, with intent to defraud, shall put ... upon any chattel or article, or upon any cask, bottle ... or other thing, any false description, statement, or other indication of or respecting the number, quantity, measure, or weight of such chattel or article, or of the place or country in which such chattel or article shall have been made, manufactured, or produced, or shall put ... any word, letter, figure, signature, or mark for the purpose of falsely indicating such chattel or article ... to be the subject of any existing patent, privilege, or copyright, shall for every such offence forfeit and pay to Her Majesty a sum equal to the value of the chattel or article and a further sum not exceeding five pounds and not less than ten shillings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers false indications of quantity, origin, patent or other intellectual-property status when done with intent to defraud; penalties mirror those for forged marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence: Selling/exposing articles with false statements of quantities, etc., on exhibit frames or displays (s.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who ... shall sell, utter, or expose for sale any chattel or article upon which shall have been, to his knowledge, put ... any false description, statement, or other indication of or respecting the number, quantity, measure, or weight ... shall for every such offence forfeit and pay to Her Majesty a sum not exceeding five pounds and not less than five shillings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets false statements on cases, frames, or other things used to exhibit goods; lesser minimum penalty (5s) compared to s.4/7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proviso: Use of generic class names or expressions not to be construed as offence (s.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided always, that the provisions of this act shall not be construed so as to make it any offence for any person to apply to any chattel or article ... any name, word, or expression for indicating such chattel or article to be of some particular class or description of manufacture only, or so generally used as to make it any offence for any person to sell, utter, or expose for sale any chattel or article to which any such generally used name, word, or expression shall have been applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits use of generic descriptors indicating class of manufacture; does not criminalize ordinary descriptive labelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of pleading: 'trade mark' and 'forged or counterfeit trade mark' need not be further described (s.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: In every indictment, pleading, proceeding, and document whatsoever in which any trade mark shall be intended to be mentioned it shall be sufficient to mention or state the same to be a trade mark without further or otherwise describing such trade mark, or setting forth any copy or fac-simile thereof; similarly for forged or counterfeit trade marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifies prosecutorial and pleading requirements; courts need not require detailed reproductions of marks in pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction not to prejudice civil remedies nor force admissibility of compelled disclosure (s.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions ... concerning any act ... shall not take away, diminish, or prejudicially affect any suit, process, proceeding, right, or remedy which any person aggrieved by such act may be entitled to at law, in equity, or otherwise ... provided always, that no evidence, statement, or discovery which any person shall be compelled to give or make shall be admissible in evidence against such person in support of any indictment for a misdemeanor ... or of any proceeding under the provisions of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal prosecution under the Act coexists with civil remedies; compelled civil disclosures are protected from being used in criminal prosecutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent: need not be to defraud a particular person; allegation/proof rules (s.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it shall be necessary to allege or mention an intent to defraud, it shall be sufficient to allege that the person did such act with intent to defraud, or to enable some other person to defraud, without alleging intent to defraud any particular person; and it shall not be necessary to prove an intent to defraud any particular person, but only that the accused did the act with intent to defraud or to enable some person to defraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowers the prosecutorial burden with respect to identifying a specific victim; intent may be general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary liability: aiding, abetting, counselling, or procuring offences (s.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who shall aid, abet, counsel, or procure the commission of any offence which is by this act made a misdemeanor shall also be guilty of a misdemeanor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons who assist or facilitate main offenders are criminally liable under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment for misdemeanors under the Act (s.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who shall be convicted or found guilty of any offence which is by this act made a misdemeanor shall be liable, at the discretion of the court, to suffer such punishment by imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, with or without hard labour, and also by fine, and also by imprisonment until the fine (if any) shall have been paid and satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides maximum custodial term (2 years) and discretionary fines; courts may order combined penalties and imprisonment in default of fine payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of penalties and civil enforcement procedures (s.15--17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties and sums forfeited to Her Majesty may be recovered in England and Wales or Ireland in an action of debt by any person as plaintiff on behalf of Her Majesty; amounts may be determined by jury or court; alternatively, in England and Wales by summary proceeding before two justices; in Scotland by action before Court of Session or summary action before sheriff with poinding warrant provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies jurisdictions, procedural routes (action of debt or summary proceedings), entitlement to costs, and enforcement mechanisms akin to other monies payable to the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary recovery procedures and applicable summary-conviction statute (s.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: When penalties are sought to be recovered by summary proceeding before two justices of the peace, the offence shall be deemed to be within the meaning of the statute (12 & 13 Vict.) to facilitate justices' duties with respect to summary convictions and orders; information, conviction and proceedings shall be had according to that act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows summary route for quicker recovery; follow the referenced summary convictions statute for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation period for actions to recover penalties or procure conviction (s.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall commence any action or proceeding for the recovery of any penalty, or procuring the conviction of any offender ... after the expiration of three years next after the committing of the offence, or one year next after the first discovery thereof by the person proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory limitation: three years from offence or one year from first discovery for actions by private persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor warranty: vendor deemed to warrant that the trade mark is genuine (s.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person shall sell or contract to sell any chattel or article with any trade mark thereon ... the sale or contract to sell shall be deemed to have been made with a warranty or contract by the vendor to the vendee that every trade mark upon such chattel or article was genuine and true, and not forged or counterfeit, and not wrongfully used, unless the contrary be expressed in writing signed by or on behalf of the vendor and delivered to and accepted by the vendee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes implied warranty of genuineness on sellers unless disclaimed in signed writing; protects buyers and supports civil remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor warranty: vendor deemed to warrant that quantity/description was true (s.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person shall sell or contract to sell any chattel or article upon which any description, statement, or other indication of number, quantity, measure, weight, or place/country of manufacture has been applied, the sale shall be deemed to have been made with a warranty by the vendor that no such description was in any material respect false or untrue, unless the contrary be expressed in signed writing delivered to and accepted by the vendee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel implied warranty for quantity and origin descriptions; protect buyers from false descriptive claims unless disclaimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil remedies: courts may order destruction, injunctions, inspection, and contempt for disobedience (s.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any suit at law or in equity against any person for forging or counterfeiting any trade mark ... the Court shall have power to direct every such chattel and article to be destroyed or otherwise disposed of; the court may award injunctions to command defendants to forbear repetition; the court may order inspection of manufacture or processes and of instruments used; refusal or neglect to obey such order is contempt of court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables comprehensive civil relief including destruction of infringing goods, injunctive relief, orders for inspection of processes/manufactures, and contempt sanctions for non-compliance.
